records.title: BRCA2 C-terminal clamp restructures RAD51 dimers to bind B-DNA for replication fork stability
records.abstract: Tumor suppressor protein breast cancer susceptibility protein 2 (BRCA2) acts with RAD51 in replication fork protection (FP) and homology-directed DNA-break repair (HDR). Critical for cancer etiology and therapy resistance, the BRCA2 C terminus was thought to stabilize recombinogenic RAD51 after the assembly of ATP-extended RAD51 filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). Here, the detailed crystal structure of the human BRCA2 C-terminal interaction domain (TR2 interface [TR2i]) complexed with ATP-bound RAD51 prior to DNA binding instead reveals TR2i unexpectedly induces a unique ATP-RAD51 dimer conformation that accommodates nucleation onto double-stranded B-DNA unsuited for HDR initiation. Structural, biochemical, and molecular results with interface-guided mutations uncover TR2i’s FP mechanism. Proline-driven secondary structure stabilizes residue triads and spans the RAD51 dimer, engaging pivotal interactions of RAD51 M210 and BRCA2 S3291/P3292, the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation site that toggles between FP during S phase and HDR in G2. TR2i evidently acts as an allosteric clamp, switching RAD51 from ssDNA to double-stranded and B-DNA binding, enforcing FP over HDR, challenging the current BRCA2-RAD51 dogma.

records.title: A Comprehensive Review on Thyroid Management And Therapeutic Potential of Medicinal Plants
records.abstract: Thyroid diseases are widespread endocrine disorders that affect a significant portion of the global population. The pathology associated with specific types or stages of thyroid disease is complex and intricately linked to various biological functions. While the mortality rate associated with thyroid dysfunction is relatively low, it can lead to metabolic and immunological disorders that result in considerable discomfort for affected individuals. Currently, numerous pharmaceutical options are available for managing thyroid disease; however, issues such as drug toxicity and prolonged treatment durations highlight the urgent need for more effective alternatives. Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent endocrine conditions worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups and contributing significantly to morbidity and reduced quality of life. Effective thyroid management requires accurate diagnosis, appropriate therapeutic interventions, and long-term monitoring to prevent complications and optimize patient outcomes.

records.title: Water Lily or Camelotte Sign in Pulmonary Hydatid Cyst – An Orphan Disease
records.abstract: A 20 – year – old male without any previous comorbidity presented to pulmonary medicine outpatient department with complaints of dull aching chest pain on right side, dry cough and shortness of breath for the pastone year. He was non vegetarian and had no addictions. On general physical examination his vitals were stableand respiratory system examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right hemithorax. All his routineblood investigations were normal. Chest radiograph revealed homogenous opacity in the right middle andlower zones. Contrast enhanced computed tomography of thorax and abdomen showed a well defined encapsulatedcystic lesion of size 12x10x14cm with internal floating membranes (water lily sign or Camelotte sign) with masseffect on adjacent lung parenchyma causing atelectasis and compression of adjacent vessels (Figure 1). Hydatid serology (IgG) was positive. Patient was treated symptomatically and referred for surgical intervention.

records.title: Aromatic polyketides from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus unguis PM03: α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, structure-activity relationship, molecular docking and ADMET evaluation
affiliations: Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology
Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
Trường Đại học Khoa học Sức khỏe
records.abstract: Chemical investigation of Aspergillus unguis PM03 yielded eight known aromatic polyketides, including unguinol (1), nidulin (2), 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3), 2-chlorounguinol (4), emeguisin B (5), aspergillusether A (6), guisinol (7), and isosclerone (8). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and comparison with published data. All isolated compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against four human cancer cell lines (KB, Hep-G2, A549, and MCF-7) and for α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. None of the compounds exhibited significant cytotoxicity (IC50 > 128 μM). Compounds 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 inhibited α-glucosidase, with guisinol (7) showing the strongest activity (IC50 = 4.01 μM), followed by isosclerone (8) (11.39 μM), emeguisin B (5) (24.31 μM), unguinol (1) (26.28 μM), and 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3) (28.83 μM). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the α-glucosidase inhibitory activity of compounds 1–7. A preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis suggested that the substitution pattern of the aromatic polyketides may affect their inhibitory activity. Molecular docking of compounds 1–7 and four aromatic polyketides previously isolated in our studies was performed against penicillin-binding protein 2a (PBP2a; PDB ID: 1MWT), together with in silico ADMET prediction to assess their pharmacokinetic properties.

records.title: Analysis of blood components and the mechanism of anti-pharyngitis and gut microbiota regulation in Ardisia crenata and its relatives
records.abstract: This study comprehensively integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and gut microbiota analysis to explore the anti-pharyngitis targets and pathways of Ardisia crenata Sims (ZSG), Ardisia crenata Sims var.bicolor (Walk) (HLS) and Ardisiacrispa (Thunb.) (BLJ), and to investigate their underlying mechanisms. PPI networks and “herb-component-target-disease” networks were constructed, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analysis. Molecular docking demonstrated strong binding affinity between the active components and the core targets. Additionally, changes in gut microbiota and endogenous metabolites in rats were analyzed by combining 16S rDNA high-throughput sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. The results revealed that the central targets are SRC, TNF, PIK3CA, STAT3, JAK2. KEGG analysis highlighted notable involvement of the PI3K/AKT, Rap1, Ras, Estrogen signaling pathways. Moreover, all three herbs were found to modulate the gut microbiota to some extent, contributing to the alleviation of microbial dysbiosis. In conclusion, ZSG, HLS and BLJ exert anti-pharyngitis effects through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms.

records.title: Caracterización clínica y epidemiológica de la bronquitis aguda en pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años durante 2023
records.abstract: Introducción: La bronquitis aguda es una de las infecciones respiratorias más frecuentes en la población pediátrica y representa una causa importante de consulta y hospitalización en América Latina. Metodología: Se realizó un estudio observacional, descriptivo, transversal y retrospectivo mediante revisión de historias clínicas electrónicas de 83 pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años con diagnóstico de bronquitis aguda atendidos durante enero–diciembre de 2023. Resultados: Predominó el sexo masculino (61,4%) y el grupo de 2 a 4 años (44,6%). La tos fue la manifestación más frecuente (92,8%), seguida de fiebre (62,7%) y sibilancias (51,8%). Las complicaciones más frecuentes fueron la exacerbación del asma (10,8%) y la otitis media aguda (8,4%). Los broncodilatadores inhalados fueron el tratamiento más utilizado (75,9%), seguidos de antipiréticos (72,3%); los antibióticos se emplearon en 13,3%. Conclusiones: La bronquitis aguda presentó predominio masculino, mayor frecuencia en niños de 2 a 4 años y una presentación clínica caracterizada principalmente por tos. Las complicaciones graves fueron poco frecuentes y el uso de antibióticos fue limitado.

records.title: Extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, and product development of oridonin: a review
records.abstract: Isodon rubescens (I. rubescens), a plant of the family Lamiaceae, is the dried aerial part of I. rubescens (Hemsl.) Hara. It has the effects of clearing heat and detoxifying, relieving pain, promoting blood circulation, and reducing swelling. As a highly valued traditional Chinese medicine, it contains a variety of chemical components. Among them, oridonin (ORI) exhibits antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties, garnering significant attention in pharmacological research. Furthermore, ORI serves as a crucial quality control marker for I. rubescens. It can exert biological effects on the nervous, cardiovascular, and visceral organ systems via multiple signaling pathways, thereby conferring potential therapeutic value for related diseases. To improve the efficacy and safety of its applications and ensure that the isolated monomer compounds exhibit high purity and favorable stability, the extraction and purification processes have been optimized. Synthetic ORI-derived products exhibit anti-inflammatory and antibacterial activities, which are widely used as dietary supplements and functional beverages in daily life. Therefore, this paper reviews the source, extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, derivatives, content determination, toxicity and product applications of ORI. This has updated and deepened the understanding of ORI, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for its further research.

records.title: Cytotoxic metabolites from the endophytic fungus Aspergillus costaricensis y15
records.abstract: Eleven compounds (1–11), comprising two previously undescribed tetrahydrofuran derivatives (1–2) alongside nine recognized metabolites (3–11), were separated and purified from the EtOAc extract derived from the endophytic strain Aspergillus costaricensis. The structural determination of the compounds was achieved unambiguously through NMR spectroscopy, HRESIMS, and ECD analysis. Subsequent biological evaluation assessed the cytotoxic, antimicrobial, and α-glucosidase inhibitory properties of all isolates. Compound 10 exhibited moderate potency against the cancer cell lines MCF-7 and A549, with respective IC50 values of 22.0 ± 1.2 μM and 15.5 ± 1.1 μM. Overall, this investigation expands the chemical diversity of the genus Aspergillus and highlights compound 10 as a promising structural scaffold for further anticancer drug development.

records.title: A new acylated quercetin triglycoside with anti-inflammatory activity from the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida
records.abstract: Phytochemical investigation of the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida led to the isolation of a previously undescribed acylated quercetin triglycoside (1), together with three known constituents (2–4). Their structures were established by HR-ESI-MS with 1D and 2D NMR analyses and, for the known compounds, by comparison with reported spectroscopic data. Compound 1 was elucidated as quercetin 3-O-[β-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→3)]-[α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→6)]-[2-O-(E)-p-coumaroyl]-β-D-glucopyranoside. Compounds 1–3 inhibited lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in RAW 264.7 macrophages, with IC50 values of 14.9 ± 1.7, 13.4 ± 2.6, and 37.7 ± 2.9 μM, respectively, while their CC50 values were >64 μM. 4 was cytotoxic (CC50 10.9 ± 0.7 μM) and was therefore not evaluated for nitric oxide inhibition. These findings expand the known chemical diversity of C. flavida var. flavida and identify 1 and 2 as moderate inhibitors of nitric oxide production.

records.abstract: Peptic ulcer disease remains clinically important despite effective Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) eradication and acid-suppressive therapy. Bixa orellana L. (annatto or achiote) is a tropical medicinal plant whose seed arils are rich in the apocarotenoids bixin and norbixin, whereas its leaves contain variable phenolics, flavonoids, tannins, terpenoids, alkaloids, and other constituents depending on geography, maturity, and extraction method. This critical narrative review uses a structured search and qualitative evidence-appraisal framework to evaluate extract-specific phytochemistry, direct gastric evidence, indirectly relevant gastrointestinal and vascular evidence, mechanistic plausibility, safety, quality control, and translational readiness. The available literature supports B. orellana as a biologically plausible preclinical mucosal-protective candidate, particularly for prevention of acute chemical injury; however, it does not establish clinical efficacy or chronic ulcer-healing activity. records.title: QUIMIOTERAPIA E MUCOSITE ORAL: AVALIAÇÃO DOS ESQUEMAS E CLASSIFICAÇÃO DAS LESÕES
records.abstract: Chemotherapy is widely used in the treatment of malignant neoplasms but is associated with significant adverse effects, such as oral mucositis (OM), which compromises patient’ quality of life. This review aims to analyze the main chemotherapy regimens associated with the occurrence of oral mucositis (OM), as well as the main agents involved in the development of lesions. This integrative review was conducted between March and May 2025, searching the PubMed, SciELO, and LILACS databases. Nine clinical studies were selected that analyzed different chemotherapy regimens and OM classifications according to the WHO, NCI-CTCAE, and JCOG scales. The highest incidence of OM was observed in protocols with antimetabolites (such as 5-FU and methotrexate), alkylating agents (such as melphalan), and monoclonal antibodies (such as panitumumab and cetuximab). The severity of the lesions varied according to the protocol, dosage, number of cycles, and clinical status of the patient. Therefore, the role of the dentist in the multidisciplinary oncology care team becomes essential for the prevention and effective management of OM during chemotherapy. Keywords: Oral Mucositis, Chemotherapy Protocols, Monoclonal Antibody.

records.abstract: Five isoprenoid flavonoids (1–5) were isolated from Sophora davidii. Notably, the absolute configuration of compound 1 and the 13C NMR data of compound 4 are presented herein for the first time. The structures of all compounds were established by spectroscopic data analysis, including HR-ESI-MS, 1D NMR, and 2D NMR. Their absolute configurations were determined via theoretical calculations, including ECD and NMR chemical shift calculations. The cytotoxic effects of the isolated compounds on human HCT-116, MDA-MB-231, and BCPAP cells were evaluated using the MTT assay. Compounds 2, 3, and 5 exhibited cytotoxicity against all three cell lines, with IC50 values ranging from 10.28 μM to 19.34 μM.

affiliations: School of Medicine, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, TX, USA.
records.abstract: Background Positive paediatric cancer treatment outcomes in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs) significantly lag behind those in high-income countries. One reason for this disparity is high treatment abandonment rates in LMICs, defined as a failure to start or complete curative-intent therapy after a cancer diagnosis. We did a systematic review and meta-analysis to describe interventions aimed at reducing treatment abandonment in paediatric patients with cancer in LMICs. Methods In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we completed a comprehensive search of MEDLINE Ovid, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane on Oct 21, 2022, with an updated search on Oct 21, 2025. Studies were included if they met the following criteria: studied an intervention on treatment abandonment; included patients with cancer aged 18 years and younger; were conducted in LMICs as defined by the World Bank income classification; contained quantification of treatment abandonment by patients in a comparison and intervention group; and had a full-text article available. We restricted inclusion to English-language studies. We systematically assessed the quality of the studies and conducted a random-effects meta-analysis of risk ratios. Findings Among the 2263 articles identified across the two searches, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. records.title: Evolution of Food Science: Bridging Tradition and Innovation
records.journal: International Journal of Research and Review
records.abstract: Food science has evolved from indigenous culinary wisdom and ancient preservation methods into a complex interdisciplinary field that integrates modern technological advancements, systems biology, and data analytics. This transformation reflects a continuous interplay between traditional knowledge systems and cutting-edge scientific innovation aimed at addressing contemporary global challenges including nutrition security, public health, and environmental sustainability. This chapter comprehensively examines the historical foundations of food science, its scientific milestones, and contemporary innovations such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and personalized nutrition. Further, it highlights integrative approaches that meld traditional practices with novel technologies, supported by illustrative case studies. Ethical considerations surrounding intellectual property and cultural stewardship are discussed alongside future directions emphasizing systems thinking, resilience, and equity. This synthesis articulates a pathway toward sustainable, ethical, and health-promoting food systems at the nexus of tradition and innovation. Keywords: food science, traditional knowledge, food innovation, biotechnology, functional foods, nutrigenomics, sustainability, food safety, culinary heritage

records.title: Nasal in-situ Transferosomes as a Platform Technology for Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
records.journal: Galore International Journal of Health Sciences and Research
records.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. Keywords: Transferosomes, in-situ gel, Intranasal, Nose-to-brain, Blood-brain barrier, Vesicular drug delivery, Mucoadhesive systems, Brain targeting.

records.journal: European Journal of Medical and Health Sciences
records.abstract: In the last few decades, the management of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) has evolved notably. Medical therapy has become the main treatment choice, whereas surgery is mainly for patients who do not respond to medical treatment or who experience complications from BPH. Relevant studies were reviewed, and arguments both for and against early surgery for BPH were examined. The argument in favor of early surgery emphasized the advantages of surgery over medication for BPH in terms of both effectiveness and cost, as well as the potential for worse postoperative results if surgery is postponed. The perineal skin was sutured to the opened urethra, incorporating the urethral mucosal edge, corpus spongiosum adventitia, and skin edge. The dorsal urethral plate was left intact, preserving longitudinal blood flow within the corpus spongiosum. A Foley catheter was inserted through the proximal urethrotomy into the bladder. records.title: Design of an analysis application for predict demand forecasting in inventory system
records.journal: TEKNOSAINS Jurnal Sains Teknologi dan Informatika
records.abstract: Trading companies often face challenges in managing their inventory systems and finding it hard to match inventory levels with the increasing demand from consumers. This paper tries to create a system that can forecast how much of a product customers might want and also check how well different deep learning methods work. In this paper, the author uses both experimental and applied methods to check how well each deep learning algorithm works.The algorithms tested are CNN-LSTM, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer. The author used data from Kaggle that includes 76,000 sales records from 2022 up to 2024, covering different product categories such as clothing, furniture, electronics, toys, and groceries. The data was then cleaned and split into groups for training and testing. The author found the results by testing various deep learning algorithms. The top performing algorithm is CNN-LSTM, which has MAE of 28.2136, RMSE of 36.6037, and R² of 0.3106. Even though the R2 value shows the model doesn't have strong predictive power yet, it is still the best performing model out of all the ones studied in this research. By comparing the system's performance to standard operating levels, it was found that the system can adjust to changes in demand.This suggests it could help trading companies better manage their stock and offer more understanding of how deep learning models work.

records.abstract: Background: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is the only non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan of the extracellular matrix and the molecule most often invoked to justify "regenerative" injectable therapy.The same polymer is marketed as joint lubricant, volumizer, dermal biostimulator and cell-delivery scaffold.This review reconciles that promise with clinical evidence, regulatory status, product heterogeneity and price reality.Methods: Evidence was identified in a structured, non-systematic manner through PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library, citation chaining from retrieved reviews and guidelines, official regulator and manufacturer sources (United States Food and Drug Administration [FDA] premarket-approval and clearance summaries, Federal Register, European Union guidance, Brazilian National Health Surveillance Agency [ANVISA], instructions for use), payer policies, public pricing files and focused web discovery, to 9 September 2026.Exact strings and yields were not preserved; no pooling, PRISMA-based screening, protocol registration, risk-of-bias scoring or de-novo certainty grading was undertaken, and certainty is reported as published by source syntheses.This is a narrative review, not a systematic review, umbrella review or meta-analysis.

AIM To compare the incidence of PECS between intermittent electrocoagulation (I-ESD) technique and conventional continuous electrocoagulation (C-ESD) during colorectal ESD. METHODS This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent colorectal ESD at the First Affiliated Hospital of Ningbo University between November 2023 and November 2024. Procedures were performed by experienced endoscopists, with one using I-ESD and the others using C-ESD. The primary outcome was the incidence of PECS. records.title: Bitter side of sweet: A stage-dependent immunometabolic model linking metabolic syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease
records.abstract: The increasing prevalence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has prompted renewed interest in their poorly defined bidirectional relationship, underpinned by shared mechanisms such as epithelial barrier disruption, chronic low-grade inflammation, and microbial dysbiosis. In this review, we comprehensively synthesize current evidence on the relationship between MetS and IBD, highlighting their shared pathophysiological mechanisms. We further propose a biphasic model of the MetS-IBD interaction, supported by original immunological data obtained from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and concomitant MetS. Early-stage MetS appears to promote a regulatory immune phenotype characterized by increased interleukin-10 and galectin-3-related pathways, which is associated with attenuated UC, whereas advanced MetS appears to be associated with a pro-inflammatory phenotype, increased interleukin-6 and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 signaling, cytotoxic immune-cell infiltration, mucosal damage, and more severe UC. This paradigm should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires validation in independent longitudinal cohorts. Nevertheless, it provides a translational framework for future biomarker development, metabolic stratification, and stage-adapted therapeutic research in patients with IBD and metabolic comorbidity.

records.title: Small extracellular vesicles as liquid biopsy targets and precision therapeutics for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
records.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects over one-third of the global population, yet robust molecular biomarkers for early disease activity and treatment monitoring remain limited. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) carry nucleic acids, proteins, and lipids that reflect disease-associated intercellular signaling and are being investigated as liquid-biopsy analytes and therapeutic platforms. Candidate sEV miRNAs, proteins, and lipid signatures have shown potential for disease characterization, but evidence derives mainly from small, heterogeneous cohorts with limited external validation. No sEV-based assay is established for routine MASLD diagnosis, staging, or treatment monitoring. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEVs and engineered sEV platforms have shown therapeutic potential in preclinical MASLD-related models through modulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, and targeted cargo delivery, although some engineering strategies remain supported primarily by non-MASLD proof-of-concept evidence. Key barriers to translation include heterogeneity in extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization, lipoprotein co-isolation, prospective multicenter validation, and, for therapeutic products, manufacturing consistency, biodistribution, dosing, and safety. This narrative review integrates diagnostic and therapeutic evidence within an evidence-classified translational framework.

records.title: Digital Twin Models for Cancer.
affiliations: Department of Biostatistics, China Pharmaceutical University, Nanjing, China.
records.abstract: The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials.

Using this approach, we have studied the spatial organization and temporal dynamics of myeloma cells, their interactions with the immune microenvironment, and the effects of acute drug treatments. records.title: Measurable Residual Disease.
affiliations: Department of Hematopathology, ACTREC, Tata Memorial Center, HBNI University, Room 18, CCE Building, ACTREC, Sector 22, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, 410210, India. docprt@gmail.com.
records.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) serves as a critical biomarker of prognosis, treatment efficacy, and clinical outcome. It captures the presence of residual tumor cells below the detection threshold of conventional microscopy. Multiparametric flow cytometry (MFC) offers a rapid, cost-efficient, and widely applicable platform for MRD detection through leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIPs) and deviation-from-normal (DfN) antigen maturation patterns. This technique underpins a wide range of clinical applications, including risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and post-transplant surveillance. This chapter outlines essential technical parameters for achieving high-sensitivity MRD detection across hematologic malignancies such as B-ALL, T-ALL, AML, MM, and CLL. Key topics covered include material required, reagent preparation, antibody panel design, sample processing and acquisition, gating strategies, and illustrative examples. Special emphasis is given to adaptations necessary for MRD monitoring following CD19-targeted therapies in B-ALL. By integrating rigorous methodology with evolving innovations, MFC continues to advance as a precise and expedient tool for MRD assessment, contributing significantly to personalized treatment strategies.

records.abstract: Cancer progression is driven by complex interactions between metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Cancer cells undergo profound metabolic adaptations that enable them to sustain rapid proliferation, maintain redox balance, and survive under conditions of hypoxia, nutrient deprivation, and cellular stress. Although aerobic glycolysis is a recognized feature of many tumors, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) remains essential in numerous cancer types, contributing to ATP production, biosynthetic pathways, and metabolic flexibility. These complementary energy-generating mechanisms allow malignant cells to adapt to changing microenvironmental conditions and maintain tumor growth.The tumor microenvironment further shapes cancer metabolism through interactions among malignant cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, immune cells, endothelial cells, and extracellular matrix components. Hypoxia-inducible signaling, nutrient competition, lactate accumulation, and altered lipid and amino acid metabolism can promote angiogenesis, immune evasion, invasion, and metastatic dissemination. In addition, metabolic communication between tumor cells and surrounding stromal cells can influence mitochondrial activity, inflammatory signaling, and resistance to anticancer treatments. records.journal: Journal of Defence Science Engineering & Technology
records.abstract: The usage of immunomodulators and immunosuppressants in critically ill COVID-19 patients increase the risk for opportunistic infections such as fungaemia. Trichosporon asahii is a yeast-like basidiomycete normally found in soil, plants, and birds that could cause rare, invasive trichosporonosis in immunocompromised patients. A 74-year-old man with comorbid dyslipidaemia and hypertension who completed two doses of COVID-19 vaccination was initially admitted for ascending cholangitis. He was infected with COVID-19 on the sixth day of admission and deteriorated, which required intubation with intensive care, and started on high-dose steroids as well as immunomodulators. However, he developed a multidrug-resistant nosocomial infection with T. asahii fungaemia. Antifungals fluconazole and voriconazole were started, while the steroid was tapered down. The patient succumbed to multiple organ dysfunction and acute respiratory distress syndrome despite aggressive management in the ICU. Fungaemia by T. asahii is a threat to critically ill COVID-19 patients despite treatment with antifungal agents proven to be effective, which warrants further research for more refined management guidelines and to identify alternative therapies to improve patients’ survival.

records.title: Majority Filter For Enhancing Pixel-Based Random Forest Land Cover Classification In Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency
records.abstract: High-quality land cover data are essential for environmental policy, spatial planning, and ecosystem monitoring. However, pixel-based classification methods, while widely used due to their practicality, often suffer from salt-and-pepper noise, which undermines map reliability. This study aimed to integrate Random Forest (RF) classification and majority filtering to enhance the quality of land cover mapping in Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency. RF was applied to Sentinel-2 image data with varying numbers of trees (ntree) to determine the optimal model performance. Subsequently, majority filtering was applied to each classification result to reduce noise and improve spatial coherence. The evaluation employed multiple accuracy metrics, including User’s Accuracy (UA), Producer’s Accuracy (PA), F1-Score, Overall Accuracy (OA), and Kappa Coefficient (KC). Comprehensive accuracy increased with the ntree until reaching an optimal point. Beyond this point, additional ntree resulted in diminishing returns. Applying majority filtering as a post-processing procedure led to further improvements in classification accuracy. While majority filtering can reduce classification noise and improve the visual quality of land cover maps, it also carries the risk of removing small, accurately classified land cover patches. records.abstract: Tumor-treating fields (TTFields) are low-intensity, intermediate-frequency alternating electric fields that convert physical energy into biological stress within dividing cancer cells. Initially recognized for their ability to disrupt mitosis, TTFields are now understood to influence a broader range of cancer-related processes, including DNA replication, repair pathways, cellular organization, and immunogenic cell death. These mechanisms are particularly relevant to gastrointestinal malignancies, where deep anatomy, stromal barriers, organ motion, peritoneal dissemination, and cumulative systemic toxicity limit conventional treatment escalation. Pancreatic cancer is currently the leading gastrointestinal indication for TTFields. In the PANOVA-3 trial, TTFields combined with standard chemotherapy improved overall survival without additional systemic toxicity, although tumor shrinkage and conventional progression-free survival remained unchanged. Evidence in hepatocellular, gastric, biliary tract, and colorectal cancers remains preliminary and should be interpreted as mechanistic or hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing. records.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in gastrointestinal malignancies: Friend or foe?
records.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), chromatin-based webs released by activated neutrophils, were first described as antimicrobial scaffolds, but these structures now appear in sterile inflammation, thrombosis, and cancer. In gastrointestinal malignancies, experimental and clinical studies have connected NETs with tumor growth, immune escape, cancer-associated thrombosis, postoperative recurrence, and metastatic spread. NET-derived DNA, histones, neutrophil elastase, myeloperoxidase, and citrullinated histones can remodel the tumor microenvironment, shield tumor cells from cytotoxic lymphocytes, promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition, awaken dormant cells, and help metastatic cells colonize distant organs. However, NETs are not simply harmful. They remain part of host defense and may restrain tumor cells in selected inflammatory, infectious, or treatment-related settings. This review summarizes NET biology in colorectal, gastric, hepatocellular, pancreatic, and other gastrointestinal cancers, focusing on the therapies that inhibit NET formation, degrade NET scaffolds, or block NET-tumor cell interactions.

records.title: Extracellular vesicles in gastrointestinal diseases: A narrative minireview of translational readiness
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate communication among epithelial, immune, stromal, microbial, and tumor compartments in gastrointestinal diseases. This narrative minireview integrates inflammatory bowel disease and major gastrointestinal malignancies (colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and liver cancers) using a five-stage translational-readiness framework: Discovery, analytical validation, clinical validation, regulatory development, and implementation. We distinguish discovery-stage and preclinical findings from clinically validated applications. EV cargo and engineered EV platforms show potential for biomarker panels, liquid biopsy, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine, but no broad EV assay or therapeutic platform is established for routine precision gastroenterology. Key barriers include pre-analytical variability, isolation-dependent results, incomplete cargo attribution, cohort heterogeneity, limited independent validation, and manufacturing and safety requirements. Progress will require standardized workflows, disease-specific comparators, prospective multicenter validation, and evidence-calibrated integration of EV data with conventional biomarkers and multi-omics.

affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important treatment option for gastric cancer, but therapeutic responses remain highly heterogeneous. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ), a major risk factor for gastric carcinogenesis, may continue to influence tumor immunity and immunotherapy outcomes after cancer develops. However, current clinical findings are inconsistent, and the biomarker value of H. pylori remains uncertain. This review critically summarizes the clinical and mechanistic evidence linking H. pylori status to ICI outcomes in gastric cancer. Potential mechanisms include regulation of programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 signaling, T-cell function, antigen presentation, myeloid immunosuppression, and microbial ecology. The divergent clinical results may reflect differences in infection status, detection methods, tumor molecular subtypes, disease stage, treatment setting, and previous therapeutic exposures. Current evidence does not support H. pylori as a validated predictive biomarker for ICI response. Rather, it may represent a context-dependent indicator of the tumor-immune-microbial background. Prospective longitudinal studies with standardized definitions of current active infection, previous infection of uncertain current status, successfully eradicated infection, and no evidence of previous infection are needed to determine whether specific H. pylori -related biological states modify the relative benefit of immunotherapy.

records.abstract: The epidemiology of gastric cancer is changing in Western populations. Population growth and ageing are projected to increase absolute case numbers despite declining age-standardised incidence, while historical registry data suggest changes in the relative contribution of diffuse-type disease, subject to period and coding effects. These trends give renewed urgency to understanding a cancer whose biology challenges established care. This narrative minireview examines the resulting gaps in prevention, diagnosis, staging and treatment of sporadic diffuse-type gastric cancer. records.title: Tumor-associated macrophages in gastric cancer: Phenotypic plasticity and therapeutic targets
affiliations: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences
records.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant, functionally plastic cells within the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment and influence tumor growth, invasion, metastasis, angiogenesis, immune evasion, chemoresistance, and metabolic reprogramming. The M1/M2 dichotomy incompletely describes TAM states; single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies have identified specialized populations that vary with tumor subtype, anatomical niche, and disease stage. This review synthesizes current evidence on TAM origin, recruitment, adaptation, and roles in malignant progression, and examines TAM-directed therapeutic strategies. TAM composition and polarization, rather than total macrophage density, may be more relevant to treatment response. Although TAM-targeting approaches show promise in preclinical models, direct clinical targeting in gastric cancer remains limited. Defining subtype-specific TAM states, clarifying microbiota-TAM interactions, and developing predictive biomarkers may advance precision immunotherapy.

records.title: SSDHR classifier network for brain tumor detection using MRI images
records.journal: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)
records.abstract: Brain tumors are the chaotic growth of abnormal brain cells, which is the main cause of cancer worldwide. Symptoms vary depending on tumor size and location, and these tumors can be cancerous or non-cancerous. Early detection and characterization are crucial but challenging due to the brain's complex structure. This study proposes a self-supervised classification deep hierarchical reconstruction network (SSDHR), a combination of generative and discriminative models. This network uses convolutional Kernels of different sizes for processing of input data on separate branches to extract effective discriminative features. A parallel-structured symmetric fusion attention (SFA) module is introduced, combining attention mechanisms for coordinates, time, and frequency to enhance the model's comprehension and feature selection. The SSDHR classifier network achieves the highest accuracy (91.9%) among 10 state-of-the-art classifiers, classifying tumors into 4 classes: pituitary, meningioma, glioma, and no tumor. The model's performance is evaluated using various metrics that demonstrate its effectiveness in brain tumor classification.

records.title: Breast cancer screening in Europe and the role of general practitioners: A 32-country comparative survey.
records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: Introduction Breast cancer is the commonest cancer in women, and screening can allow earlier-stage diagnosis. While there are European recommendations on the age-range and frequency of breast cancer screening, participation in these programmes varies substantially, and this could be due to differences in how they are organised and implemented. The role that primary healthcare professionals play in the process is unclear.We aimed to describe the breast cancer screening programmes in European countries and investigate how primary healthcare professionals are involved in this screening process.Methods A cross-sectional survey in 32 countries. Key informants with relevant expertise answered online questions about the characteristics of their screening programmes and general practitioners' (GPs') roles in this. Responses were refined through an iterative consensus process. Data were examined to identify patterns in GP engagement.Results We found important differences between European breast cancer screening systems. While most had population-based screening, four countries relied on opportunistic screening. In 15 countries GPs had little or no involvement in the process of breast cancer screening, and in 13 countries GPs had some involvement, including identifying eligible patients, issuing referrals, and following-up results. Screening uptake rates tended to be higher in countries with well-established population-based screening programmes which give little or no GP involvement.

records.abstract: This review evaluates the application of deep learning (DL) for the predictive modeling of electronic materials in computer engineering. We analyzed peer-reviewed literature across four major databases, focusing exclusively on advanced architectures like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Generative models. Results indicate these models accurately predict critical properties, such as band gaps and thermal conductivity, for next-generation semiconductors, 2D materials, and memristors. These high accuracies are achieved because architectures like GNNs effectively capture complex 3D spatial interactions without requiring manual feature engineering. However, practical fabrication remains hindered by data scarcity, algorithmic opacity, and a profound "Sim-to-Real Gap". While DL accelerates predictive design, sustaining Moore's Law ultimately requires developing autonomous "Self-Driving Labs" and Large Material Models to bridge digital predictions with physical synthesis.

affiliations: Walter Reed Army Institute of Research
records.abstract: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. These injuries not only disrupt tissues structurally but also trigger systemic cascades involving immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, and premature cellular senescence. Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: AIMS: Tumour budding (TB) has been recognized as an additional prognostic factor in the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classification systems. However, its prognostic impact in stages II and III colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inconsistently defined. This study aims to systematically evaluate the prognostic value of high-grade TB in stage II-III CRC. Multivariable analysis confirmed the independent prognostic value of high-grade TB for all three outcomes. Subgroup analysis stratified by TNM stage revealed that high-grade TB consistently predicted adverse outcomes in both stage II and stage III disease. CONCLUSIONS: This study confirms that high-grade TB is an independent prognostic factor in stage II-III CRC, consistently associated with worse DFS, OS and CSS. records.abstract: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich layer formed by glycoproteins, glycolipids, proteoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans at the outer cell surface. These changes affect how tumor cells sense force, bind the extracellular matrix, cluster receptors, evade immune surveillance, survive in circulation, and arrest at distant vascular beds. records.abstract: Esophageal candidiasis is commonly associated with HIV infection but also occurs in patients without HIV. This systematic review aimed to summarize risk factors for esophageal candidiasis in non-HIV patients. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect were searched for studies evaluating risk factors in non-HIV populations or reporting non-HIV subgroups separately, and the findings were synthesized qualitatively. Reported prevalence among non-HIV patients ranged from 0.34% to 8.99%, depending on the population and case ascertainment. Dysphagia and odynophagia predicted esophageal candidiasis in one prospective study, whereas a retrospective study found no correlation between symptoms and endoscopic severity. records.title: Triage models for surgical decision-making in patients with shoulder pain: an integrative review.
records.abstract: Shoulder pain is a major cause of work absenteeism, affecting 1 in 3 adults. Although nonsurgical treatments like physical therapy are recommended as the first line of management, 40% of patients are referred for surgery before exploring these options. This review aimed to identify existing triage models used for shoulder pain referrals for surgery, guidelines for shoulder pain management that include criteria for surgical referral, and indications for surgery. An integrative review approach was used to comprehensively search major databases (Medline, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL Plus) and gray literature. Articles on triage models, referral processes, or surgery candidacy for shoulder pain were included. The searches retrieved 4510 articles, with 480 selected for full review and 71 articles included in this synthesis. Thirty-seven articles described various triage models and clinical decision-making processes for managing shoulder pain, including determining when to refer for surgical consultation and the indications for surgery. Seventeen articles compared surgical and nonsurgical treatments to identify surgical indicators, 10 articles examined factors affecting decision-making, and 7 articles explored predictor models for surgical outcomes. The findings underscore the need for a multifactorial decision-making process that acknowledges the complexity of pain within a biopsychosocial framework and incorporates patients' personal preferences into the triage decision-making process.

records.abstract: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. This would suggest that hormones have a different effect on males and females, leading to differences in the cannabinoid’s pain-relieving ability. records.title: Thiolutin alleviates acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) in a mouse model of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Microbiology and Epidemiology
records.abstract: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) is a major, life-threatening complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and the development of novel molecular-targeted therapies for aGVHD is urgently needed. Thiolutin (THL), a disulfide-containing antibiotic, inhibits the activity of the BRCC3-containing isopeptidase complex and thereby suppresses NLR pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. Here, we investigated the effect of THL on aGVHD in a mouse model of allo-HSCT. We found that THL significantly improved survival in aGVHD recipients, reduced weight loss and clinical scores, and attenuated pathological changes in aGVHD target organs, including the liver, small intestine, and colon. Furthermore, THL diminished donor T-cell activation and infiltration into target organs and promoted the expansion of regulatory T cells. THL also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin (IL)-2, IL-17A, and IL-1β. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of THL in regulating aGVHD and highlights its potential as an anti-inflammatory therapeutic agent for clinical development in patients undergoing allo-HSCT.

Interestingly, in these systems, disruption of mRNA localization alone is enough to reduce migratory efficiency, suggesting that RNA localization itself plays an important role in regulating migration. records.abstract: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era. This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer therapies, rather than summarizing therapeutic efficacy. records.title: [Advances in precision management of aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia in breast cancer].
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College
records.abstract: Endocrine therapy is a core strategy throughout the management of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, substantially reducing the risks of recurrence and death. However, treatment-related adverse events, particularly aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia (AIA), have become a major barrier to treatment adherence. Current evidence suggests that AIA cannot be explained solely by estrogen deprivation. T-cell leukemia/lymphoma 1A (TCL1A) genetic variants, interleukin-17/nuclear factor-κB-related inflammatory pathways, and an imbalance between T helper 17 and regulatory T cells may jointly contribute to its development, suggesting that AIA may represent a modifiable pathological process. Accordingly, its management should shift from symptom-oriented palliation toward a precise supportive-care model integrating risk stratification, early intervention, and long-term adherence maintenance. From a translational medicine perspective, this review synthesizes evidence on the pathogenesis of AIA, intervention trials, and the latest guidelines, and proposes a three-stage AIA management framework adapted to Chinese clinical practice (baseline assessment and prevention-stratified intervention-digital closed-loop follow-up). The framework emphasizes the importance of alleviating adverse events to maintain treatment adherence and improve long-term outcomes but requires prospective clinical validation.

records.abstract: Copper metabolism MURR1 domain‑containing protein 1 (COMMD1) is one of the best‑characterised members of the COMMD protein family. Initially identified as a key regulator of copper ion homeostasis, accumulating evidence has shown that COMMD1 does not function as a canonical tumour suppressor or oncogene in malignant tumours. Instead, it serves as a context‑dependent molecular hub whose activity is dynamically influenced by cellular background, signalling pathway status and post‑translational modifications. On the one hand, COMMD1 exerts antitumour effects by inhibiting NF‑κB and hypoxia‑inducible factor‑1 signalling, regulating DNA damage repair, modulating cell cycle progression and enhancing apoptotic sensitivity. Conversely, in certain tumour types, COMMD1 may promote drug resistance and adaptive tumour evolution by preserving DNA repair capacity, supporting cell survival or modulating ubiquitination networks. records.title: Myeloid CD209 Drives Tumor Immune Evasion and Resistance to PD-1 Blockade Through ICAM-2–Mediated T-Cell Mechanosuppression
affiliations: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
records.abstract: Resistance to PD-1–based immunotherapy remains a major challenge in cancer treatment, especially in immunologically “cold” tumors characterized by T-cell exclusion and impaired T-cell effector function. Mechanical processes impact T-cell activity, and mechanical perturbations may represent a distinct mode of immune suppression. Here, we identified CD209, a myeloid-expressed C-type lectin receptor, as a mechanosuppressive regulator of antitumor T-cell immunity. CD209 was selectively enriched in tumor-infiltrating M2-like macrophages and monocytes, and elevated CD209 expression was associated with poor clinical response to PD-1 blockade and immune dysfunction and exclusion across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, CD209 directly engaged ICAM-2 on T cells and activated ROCK1–ERM signaling. This interaction increased T-cell cortical stiffness, destabilized T cell–antigen presenting cell interactions, and attenuated T-cell receptor signaling. Importantly, CD209 blockade enhanced the response to PD-1 inhibition and overcame resistance to PD-1–based immunotherapy in refractory and immunologically “cold” tumor models. affiliations: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University
records.abstract: Despite substantial advances in targeted therapeutic regimens for breast cancer (BC), clinical management remains challenging for refractory and therapy-resistant cases, especially for molecular subtypes lacking validated actionable targets. Besides, we discovered that FKBP10 was positively correlated with enhanced homologous recombination (HR)-mediated DNA repair and drove broad resistance to multiple DNA-damaging therapies, including cisplatin, ionizing radiation (IR) and PARP inhibitor. Mechanistically, FKBP10 physically interacted with the core HR repair protein RAD51 via a proline 22-containing motif. records.title: Adaptive sampling: information-guided selection for targeted long-read sequencing and epigenetic studies
affiliations: Institute of Bioorganic Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences
records.abstract: Adaptive sampling (AS) is a unique feature of nanopore sequencing that enables real-time enrichment or depletion of target molecules during the sequencing run based on their initial sequence information. AS provides a flexible and scalable alternative to conventional capture- and amplification-based approaches, while preserving long reads and the ability to detect epigenetic modifications of native DNA/RNA molecules. In this review, we summarize the principles of AS-based sequencing, explain the enrichment- and depletion-mode strategies and discuss factors affecting its performance. We further highlight the growing body of studies demonstrating the utility of AS across a diverse range of applications, such as metagenomic and microbiome research, structural variant characterization and discovery, studying repeat expansion disorders, integrated genetic and epigenetic profiling or transcriptome analysis. In these and other contexts, AS enables efficient allocation of sequencing capacity toward biologically relevant molecules, while accelerating data generation, which also makes it applicable to rapid molecular diagnostics and real-time genomic analyses in clinical practice. As nanopore sequencing continues to mature and become a standard analysis approach in many laboratories, AS is likely to evolve from a specialized enrichment strategy into a routine component of genomic, epigenomic, and transcriptomic workflows.

records.title: Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ3-iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
records.abstract: While 2- and 4-aryloxypyridines are ubiquitous in pharmaceutical molecules, efficient synthetic strategies—especially for synthesizing scaffolds with diverse multiple substituents on the pyridine core—remain limited. Here we show a hook-and-slide strategy for constructing these scaffolds, involving the in-situ generation of pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salts from pyridones and Koser’s reagent (hook, C3 selectivity), followed by an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration (slide, O selectivity). Such newly designed iodonium salts feature dual vicinal nucleophilic sites, and we demonstrate that using C2 − H imidazolium ionic liquids can exclusively transfer the aryl group to the strategic O site. This approach is transition-metal-free, scalable, and applicable to substrates with diverse electronic and steric properties or complex structures. Importantly, the resulting products retain −I and −NH 2 handles that are amenable to downstream derivatizations, enabling extensive exploration of previously inaccessible chemical space. The utility of this approach is further demonstrated through the concise synthesis of multiple pharmaceutical intermediates and a CRF 1 antagonist, CP-376395.

records.title: NKTR-255, a polymer-conjugated IL-15, enhances CAR T cell therapy by engaging endogenous antitumor immunity
affiliations: Cape Town HVTN Immunology Laboratory / Hutchinson Centre Research Institute of South Africa
records.abstract: CAR-T cells have yet to show widespread efficacy in solid tumors due in part to poor persistence and dysfunction in the tumor microenvironment. Further, heterogenous expression of target antigens can lead to escape of antigen-null tumors that resist CAR-T killing. Strategies to cooperatively boost both CAR-T and endogenous antitumor immunity may be critical for achieving durable efficacy in cancer patients. NKTR-255 is a polymer-conjugated IL-15 with extended half-life that can boost endogenous T and NK cells, as well as CD19 CAR-T cells in B cell malignancies. However, whether NKTR-255 is sufficient to overcome CAR-T dysfunction in the suppressive solid tumor microenvironment, and how NKTR-255 and CAR-Ts together re-shape endogenous antitumor immunity, is not known. records.abstract: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Candidate driver mutations were sparse and heterogeneous, distinguishing IEC-EC from peripheral T cell lymphoma following CAR T cell therapy. In the present study, AZT (NSC D-858683) and a Cu(II)-AZT complex (NSC D-858684) were evaluated by the National Cancer Institute Developmental Therapeutics Program using the NCI-60 human tumor cell line panel at a single concentration of 10 μM. records.title: Multi-Target-Directed Ligands Targeting Sigma Receptors and the Proteasome—A Holistic Strategy for Cancer Drug Discovery
records.abstract: Cancer cells employ multiple pro-survival strategies, including evasion of apoptosis and escape from immune surveillance. In particular, cancer cells can modulate intracellular calcium homeostasis and exploit sigma receptor (SR) activity to restore calcium balance. Furthermore, the positive correlation between sigma-1 receptor (S1R) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression levels suggests that S1R may also contribute to immune evasion. Cancer cells maintain proteostasis through enhanced unfolded protein response (UPR) signaling and activation of the ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS). The proteasome removes misfolded and ubiquitinated proteins, thereby preventing the accumulation of proteotoxic stress, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and cell death. Collectively, these adaptive mechanisms enable cancer cells to survive, proliferate, and invade, thereby promoting tumor progression. Although proteasome inhibitors (PIs) have been introduced into clinical practice for the treatment of multiple myeloma (MM), their therapeutic use is limited by several drawbacks, including the development of resistance and limited selectivity. Importantly, SRs play a pivotal role in UPR and UPS signaling; therefore, their modulation may compensate for the limitations associated with PI therapy. records.title: Advanced three-dimensional bioprinting for in vitro tumor model engineering: From biomimetic model construction to personalized precision medicine
records.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting technology offers a transformative approach for constructing biomimetic tumor organoid models that overcome the limitations of traditional two-dimensional cell cultures and animal models. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in 3D bioprinted tumor organoids, emphasizing extrusion-based, inkjet-based, and lithography-based bioprinting methods. These technologies enable precise spatial control of cell distribution and tissue architecture, achieving high reproducibility while maintaining complex tumor microenvironmental characteristics. Applications across multiple cancer types—including colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, breast, glioma, renal, bladder, lung, and thyroid cancers—demonstrate significant potential for drug screening, tumor heterogeneity research, and preclinical evaluation of individualized treatment responses. Despite substantial progress, challenges remain regarding multicellular complexity simulation, technical resolution, and biomaterial optimization. Future directions include integrating four-dimensional bioprinting, multiomics analysis, and immune microenvironment reconstruction to enhance physiological fidelity and clinical applicability, ultimately advancing precision oncology and personalized cancer treatment strategies.

records.title: MelanoFusion: An Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid CNN–Transformer Framework for Dermoscopic Melanoma Detection
records.abstract: Abstract Melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer requiring early detection, yet automated analysis remains affected by lesion variation, calibration errors, uncertainty, and subgroup disparities. This study presents MelanoFusion, a hybrid framework integrating explainability, uncertainty estimation, and fairness-oriented representation learning for melanoma detection. It combines EfficientNetV2-S and Swin Transformer encoders with cross-attention, lesion attention, feature-pyramid processing, multi-scale transformer layers, and an uncertainty head. Images were resized to 224 × 224 and processed using hair removal, median filtering, contrast enhancement, colour normalization, and watershed-based lesion priors; U-Net was used for lesion segmentation. MelanoFusion was evaluated against DenseNet121, ResNet101, EfficientNetV2-S, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and Swin Transformer on HAM10000, ISIC 2018, and PH². Segmentation Dice was 0.878 on HAM10000 and 0.830 on PH². MelanoFusion achieved ROC-AUC values of 0.687, 0.740, and 0.844 on HAM10000, ISIC 2018, and PH², respectively. Calibration was favourable on HAM10000, with an expected calibration error of 0.116. Uncertainty was significantly associated with classification error, while subgroup analysis showed significant sensitivity differences across age groups but not sex. records.title: Multiple Rectal Neuroendocrine Tumors Treated by Endoscopic Resection: A Case Report.
affiliations: Endoscopy Division National Cancer Center Hospital Tokyo Japan.
records.abstract: Rectal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are typically solitary, and the occurrence of multiple lesions is uncommon. We present a case of multiple rectal NETs in a 41-year-old man. Colonoscopy performed at another hospital revealed three lesions (4 mm in the sigmoid colon and 5 and 10 mm in the rectum), all of which were diagnosed as NET, grade 1 (G1), following endoscopic resection; one lesion had a positive vertical margin. Upon referral to our institution, repeat colonoscopy demonstrated multiple yellowish, slightly elevated lesions throughout the rectum, all of which were histologically confirmed as NETs. Imaging studies showed no evidence of lymph node or distant metastasis. Although additional surgical resection was considered because of the multiplicity of lesions and positive margin, the patient strongly preferred endoscopic therapy. Eight lesions were successfully resected using endoscopic mucosal resection with a cap or endoscopic submucosal dissection. Histopathological examination revealed seven NET, G1 lesions and one NET, G2 lesion. Additional surgery was recommended but was declined by the patient, and no local recurrence or distant metastasis has been observed during 18 months of follow-up. This rare case highlights the potential role and the limitations of endoscopic treatment in patients with multiple rectal NETs.

records.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. records.title: Primate-specific SSX1 is required for CPSF6-dependent spermatocyte transcription and human fertility
affiliations: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China
First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University
records.abstract: Abstract Genetic variation is a major cause of male infertility, and defining the underlying mechanisms is essential for developing effective interventions. SSX1 is a primate specific gene whose deficiency has been linked to sperm malformations in humans and cynomolgus monkeys, yet its pathogenic mechanism remains unclear. Here, by whole exome sequencing of a cohort of 536 men with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (OAT), we identified three previously unreported SSX1 variants, including two deletion alleles and one selective splice site variant. SSX1 deficiency was associated with a characteristic OAT phenotype featuring short, coiled flagella and severe loss of the central pair microtubules. SSX1 is expressed in early spermatocytes, and its loss disrupted the expression of spermiogenesis and sperm function related genes that are transcribed in advance during the spermatocyte stage. Mechanistically, SSX1 acts as a transcriptional regulator by interacting with the transcription and processing factor CPSF6 and promoting nuclear recruitment of the CPSF complex, with functional relevance in both spermatocytes and spermatids. Collectively, our study supports a functional role for SSX1 with CPSF6 in human spermatogenesis, expands the genetic diagnostic spectrum of OAT, and provides a transcription focused framework for precision management of male infertility.

Women with adenomyosis undergoing frozen embryo transfer (FET) have lower implantation and live birth rates compared to women without the disease. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (GnRH-a) pretreatment before FET has been proposed to improve reproductive outcomes by suppressing adenomyotic activity and enhancing endometrial receptivity; however, published studies have reported conflicting findings. The objective of this review was to evaluate the current evidence regarding the effectiveness of GnRH-a pretreatment before FET in women with adenomyosis. A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and SCOPUS was performed up to November 9, 2024. records.title: Identification of a golgi apparatus-related gene signature for the molecular classification of uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma
records.abstract: Abstract Background Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) lacks reliable molecular biomarkers for early detection and classification. While pathway-based prognostic models have been reported, the role of organelle dysfunction, particularly Golgi biology, remains uninvestigated. We aimed to identify Golgi apparatus-related genes (GARGs) of diagnostic value and construct a classification signature for UCEC. Methods Transcriptomic data from TCGA-UCEC (549 tumors; normal controls from TCGA and GTEx) and GEO (GSE17025, 91 tumors) were analyzed. Differentially expressed GARGs were identified, and an integrative machine learning framework was used to build a diagnostic model distinguishing UCEC from normal tissue. Overall survival association and immune infiltration (CIBERSORT) were assessed as exploratory analyses. Results A four-gene GARG signature—CDK1, CCNB2, KIF20A, and PKMYT1—was identified. It distinguished UCEC from normal tissue with an AUC of 0.703 (95% CI 0.646–0.760) in TCGA and 0.927 (95% CI 0.844–1.000) in GSE17025. In an exploratory analysis, a higher signature score was associated with shorter overall survival (log-rank P = 0.027). Immune cell composition differed between UCEC and normal tissue. The four genes were enriched in cell-cycle (G2/M) and proliferation-related pathways; KIF20A showed the largest coefficient, and CDK1 was consistently identified across independent cancer models. records.title: A systematic review of liver disease registries across the globe: design, management and sustainability practices
records.abstract: Liver disease remains a major health concern globally, especially in the Asia-Pacific region, yet many low-income countries lack robust registries to track and manage it effectively. This systematic review analyzed 139 publications covering 62 liver disease registries to assess their structure, data management, quality monitoring, and sustainability, with the goal of informing registry development in low-resource settings like the Philippines. Most registries (72.6%) focused on a single disease, primarily viral hepatitis and hepatocellular carcinoma, and were commonly found in high-income countries. National-level implementation was typical (50%), though only a third had clear governance structures, and nearly half lacked long-term funding. While half employed quality monitoring, data security measures were often unspecified. The findings underscore the vital role of liver disease registries in improving care and informing policy, while highlighting persistent gaps in governance, standardization, and sustainability.

records.abstract: Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro studies have demonstrated the anticancer potential of Vernolac and its active ingredients, safety data are available only for some of the plant ingredients of Vernolac. In the present study, acute and 28-day repeat-dose toxicity of Vernolac were evaluated in Wistar rats in accordance with OECD guidelines 420 and 407, respectively. Acute toxicity was investigated for 14 days after administering a single oral dose of 2000 mg/kg to 10 animals (5 males, 5 females). A repeat-dose toxicity study was conducted, in which the human equivalent therapeutic dose in rats (HED; 165 mg/kg/day), a mid-dose (2 × HED; 330 mg/kg/day), and a high dose (4 × HED; 660 mg/kg/day) were administered to three separate groups, each comprising 10 naive animals (5 males and 5 females), for a period of 28 days. In both acute and repeat-dose studies, no morbidity, mortality, changes in food and water intake, relative organ weights, microscopic changes in organs, hematological changes, or clinical signs of toxicity were observed. In the acute study, a significant increase in AST and ALT levels was observed in males. records.title: A simplified pre-bronchoscopy risk stratification model for patients with suspected lung cancer based on age, smoking status, and serum CEA
affiliations: First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University
records.abstract: Background Bronchoscopy is commonly used in the diagnostic work-up of patients with suspected lung cancer, yet clinicians often lack a simple tool to estimate malignancy risk before the procedure in patients already being considered for bronchoscopic evaluation. Most existing prediction models focus on the malignant potential of pulmonary nodules and rely heavily on imaging features, limiting their applicability to the pre-bronchoscopy setting. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a simplified pre-bronchoscopy risk stratification model using routinely available clinical variables. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 336 patients undergoing evaluation for suspected lung cancer. Candidate predictors were restricted to variables available before bronchoscopy and selected based on clinical relevance, routine availability, and data completeness. From 32 candidate predictors, LASSO regression retained 18 variables, which were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model followed by elimination based on statistical and clinical criteria. A simplified model was then constructed and presented as a nomogram. Model performance was assessed in the full cohort, with bootstrap internal validation using 1,000 resamples; the post-LASSO elimination steps were not repeated within bootstrap samples. records.title: Multiplexed FRET-FLIM profiling of immune checkpoint interactions predicts response to atezolizumab in urothelial carcinoma
records.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have shown great promise in treating bladder cancer and are now part of the standard treatment for advanced disease. However, many patients still fail to respond to treatment, and at present, many biomarkers are assessed but have yet shown only limited results. Therefore, with the advent of combination treatments and the increase in immune-related adverse event, the search for reliable predictive biomarkers is paramount. Using a multiplexed enhanced FRET-FLIM-based technique (QF-Pro), we quantified the interaction of PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4/CD80, and TIGIT/CD155 immune checkpoints in a pre-treatment TMA of 46 patients treated with atezolizumab. The association between higher PD-1/PD-L1 ICP interaction state and treatment efficacy was demonstrated in the male sample cohort, where it identified patients with better progression-free survival. Conversely, patients exhibiting higher CTLA-4/CD80 engagement had a worse response to atezolizumab. Remarkably, the dual assessment of patients with high PD-1/PD-L1 and low CTLA-4/CD80 allowed to identify the best responders. These results indicate that the monitoring of patients’ immune profile in urothelial carcinoma might be critical in identifying patients who may benefit from combination therapy.
