records.title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
affiliations: Southern University of Science and Technology
records.abstract: R-2-Hydroxyglutarate (R2HG), an oncometabolite predominantly produced by mutated isocitrate dehydrogenase 1/2 (IDH1/2) in various cancers, is known to drive cancer progression through noncovalent inhibition of α-ketoglutarate (αKG)-dependent enzymes. In this work, we propose an alternative mechanism wherein R2HG contributes to cancer development via covalent modification of biologically critical lysines, a process termed lysine-R2HGylation (KR2HG). We designed and synthesized R2HG-mimicking probes and demonstrated their effectiveness in facilitating KR2HG target profiling and site mapping. We identified KR2HG as a post-translational modification, confirmed its C5-linkage on GSTP1(K209), and demonstrated that SIRT5 functions as a deacylase for GSTP1-KR2HG in vitro. Furthermore, we found that R2HG slightly but significantly inhibits the enzymatic activity of GSTP1 through KR2HG and dramatically suppresses monocyte differentiation via this catalytically important lysine modification. Our findings provide an alternative perspective on the role of R2HG in leukemia progression and offer a practical tool for the clinical investigation of R2HG-elevated cancers. R-2-hydroxyglutarate is a cancer-linked metabolite whose mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, the authors identify and structurally characterize lysineR2HGylation as a protein modification and develop probes that reveal GSTP1 as a functional target in leukemia cells.

records.title: The AKAP1 ribonucleoprotein network integrates mitochondrial homeostasis, P-body dynamics and protein translation in cycling cells
affiliations: Istituto per il Sistema Produzione Animale in Ambiente Mediterraneo
records.abstract: Abstract Integration of protein translation and mitochondrial activities represents a mechanism to rapidly adapt anabolic processes to specific cellular needs. This aspect is of particular importance for cell division when mitochondrial dynamics, oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis are timely coordinated to allow a faithful completion of the cell cycle. However, the mechanisms coupling mitochondrial homeostasis to protein translation in cycling cells are largely unknown. Here, we report the identification of a molecular network assembled by AKAP1 at mitochondria that includes mRNA, components of the translation repression machinery (P-bodies) and mitotic kinases (CDK1/2). During interphase, the AKAP1 complex dynamically coordinates cAMP signaling, mitochondrial activity, P-body dynamics and protein translation to ensure proper cell cycle progression. At mitosis, CDK-induced proteolysis of AKAP1 via a cullin-mediated ubiquitin pathway reduces oxidative metabolism, promotes mitochondrial fission and reshapes mRNA translation, finalizing the cell cycle. Disruption of this network impairs cell cycle progression. These findings unveil a regulatory mechanism controlled by AKAP1 that functionally and dynamically links oxidative metabolism to protein synthesis in cycling cells. Targeting this biological node could help to restore deranged mitochondrial function during degenerative and proliferative disorders.

records.title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3 -dependent pathway
affiliations: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
records.abstract: The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in PTEN , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of Pten in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of Pten , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of Pten uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that Pten regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

records.title: Pyrrocidines and hirsutellones: distinctive fungal polyketide alkaloid hybrids with intriguing therapeutic applications: a comprehensive update
records.abstract: Covering: 2005-2025Pyrrocidines and hirsutellones are a fascinating class of fungal natural products that possess an intricate chemical structure characterized by a distinctive macrocyclic ring fused to a decahydrofluorene core. Known for their complex architectures as PKS-NRPS hybrids, these metabolites are isolated from various fungi and have attracted significant attention due to their potent pharmacological properties, including antimicrobial, antifungal, and anticancer effects. This review article aims to shed light on the structural diversities of 52 fungal-derived pyrrocidines and hirsutellones reported over the period of 2005-2025, providing insights into their chemistry, biosynthetic origins, pharmacokinetic profiles, and structure-activity relationships (SARs). Furthermore, we critically evaluate their promising therapeutic potential, highlighting the opportunities they present for modern drug discovery and development.

records.abstract: Abstract Background: Group 3 medulloblastoma (G3-MB) carries the worst prognosis, and validated therapeutic targets downstream of MYC remain limited. We investigated PRMT5-associated molecular and clinical features in G3-MB. Methods and Results: We integrated 763 bulk transcriptomes, approximately 25,000 single-nucleus RNA-seq profiles from 12 G3-MB patients, and 144 paired methylation-expression data. PRMT5 was higher in G3-MB than in SHH tumors and was independently associated with poor overall survival in an institutional validation cohort. Its expression was not associated with copy-number gain, but correlated with promoter hypomethylation and MYC/E2F1/SP1 co-expression. Network analysis placed PRMT5 in a MYC-correlated module enriched for ribosome biogenesis. At single-nucleus resolution, PRMT5-positive tumor cells showed elevated MYC and proliferation programs, although these associations were sensitive to detection threshold and library size. PRMT5-high tumors showed expression of genes linked to PRMT5-inhibitor pathways, DNA damage response, and replication stress. An exploratory seven-gene PRMT5-associated continuous score showed prognostic signal in the training and institutional validation cohorts. Conclusions: Integrated analyses associate PRMT5 with MYC-linked ribosome biogenesis and proliferative programs in G3-MB. records.title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Imaging Biomarkers for Distinguishing Pseudoprogression from True Progression after Cellular Immunotherapy in Glioblastoma
records.abstract: Abstract Pseudoprogression, transient radiographic worsening caused by treatment-related inflammation rather than tumor growth, is a well-recognized pitfall after chemoradiotherapy for glioblastoma and is becoming more relevant as checkpoint inhibitors and cellular immunotherapies such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells enter clinical testing. Conventional structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cannot reliably separate pseudoprogression from true progression, exposing patients to premature treatment discontinuation or unnecessary intensification. Quantitative, artificial-intelligence-based imaging analysis (radiomics, and its molecular extension radiogenomics) is an emerging candidate solution. In this narrative review we synthesize the evidence on radiomics and radiogenomics for differentiating pseudoprogression from true progression in glioblastoma, with emphasis on the immunotherapy and cellular-therapy context. We summarize the pathobiology and reported frequency of pseudoprogression after standard and immune-based therapies, outline the limitations of current response criteria (RANO, iRANO, RANO 2.0), and review representative studies of texture analysis, hand-crafted radiomics, deep-learning radiomics, and radiogenomics. TTFields were initiated with maintenance temozolomide after standard chemoradiation. At first radiographic progression, patients chose whether to continue or discontinue TTFields. Post-recurrence survival and overall survival from surgery were analyzed using the Kaplan–Meier method and Cox proportional hazards models. TTFields adherence (≥ 75% vs. <75%) was also evaluated. Results Of 39 TTFields-treated patients, three without recurrence and one with missing usage data were excluded, leaving 35 for analysis: 15 continued treatment after recurrence and 20 discontinued it. records.abstract: Introduction The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR), initially characterized as a sensor of environmental toxicants, is now recognized as an important regulator of innate immunity and macrophage biology. Although AHR has been shown to influence macrophage polarization and the differentiation of human monocytes into monocyte-derived macrophages or dendritic cells, the molecular and metabolic mechanisms underlying AHR activation in primary human macrophages remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to investigate the effects of AHR activation on the functional, transcriptional, and metabolic profiles of human monocyte-derived macrophages. Methods Human monocyte-derived macrophages were treated with the xenobiotic AHR ligand 6-formylindolo[3,2-b]carbazole (FICZ). records.title: 3D ultrasound shear wave elastography quantifies myocardial stiffness and anisotropy in the human heart
affiliations: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
records.abstract: Abstract Myocardial stiffness (MS) is a key property of diastolic cardiac function which is altered in various cardiomyopathies. Its quantitative evaluation remains challenging due to the myocardium’s complex anisotropic fibers architecture and dynamic contraction. We developed a novel 3D shear wave elastography (3D-SWE) system suitable for clinical translation based on 3D ultrafast volumetric imaging for the quantitative assessment of MS in the human heart. Validation was performed on calibrated phantoms and ex vivo in porcine hearts compared to standard 2D-SWE. In vivo feasibility was demonstrated on healthy volunteers and patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (CA). We demonstrated that 3D shear wave propagation can be observed in vivo and that 3D-SWE provides quantitative assessment of myocardium anisotropy through shear wave velocities along and across fibers and fractional anisotropy. In addition, MS was significantly elevated in CA patients compared to normal myocardium, whereas the fractional anisotropy was decreased. The feasibility of volumetric MS mapping on the human heart was demonstrated showing the potential of 3D-SWE as a clinically oriented tool for early diagnosis of cardiomyopathies such as CA.

records.abstract: Widely prevalent worldwide and increasingly noted in China, adjustment disorder (AD) is frequently featured on short-video apps; however, because platforms like TikTok, Bilibili, and RedNote lack robust regulation of health content, the potential for inaccurate information is high, motivating our systematic comparison of the quality of AD-related videos across these three platforms. We conducted a cross-sectional content analysis of publicly available Mandarin videos retrieved with the keyword “适应障碍” (adjustment disorder). From the top 100 search results on each platform, 228 unique videos were included (Tiktok 78; Bilibili 62; RedNote 88). Two raters evaluated overall quality (Global Quality Score, GQS 1–5), reliability (modified DISCERN, 0–5), source credibility (JAMA, 0–4), and educational usability (PEMAT-Understandability and- Actionability, 0–100%). Content completeness was coded across six domains (epidemiology, etiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, prevention) to create a Content Completeness Index (CCI, 0–12). Between-group comparisons used non-parametric tests; proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression examined independent factors associated with higher GQS and mDISCERN. records.abstract: Background: Imaging-based breast cancer risk prediction models primarily use full-field digital mammography (FFDM). Although digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) has become a predominant screening modality in the United States, its potential for long-term breast cancer risk prediction remains underexplored. Objective: The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a deep learning model that uses longitudinal DBT examinations to predict long-term breast cancer risk. Methods: This retrospective study included 313,335 DBT examinations from 161,077 women (mean age, 58.5 ± 11.7 years) between January 2016 and August 2020 at a single health institution. Model performance was compared with a single-timepoint DBT model, the Mirai model using same-day FFDM, and the Tyrer-Cuzick model using the AUC, time-dependent concordance index, and integrated Brier score. records.title: Human mitochondrial DNA variants influence telomere length
records.abstract: Telomere shortening is a hallmark of aging, yet telomere length (TL) varies considerably between individuals and is strongly influenced by inheritance. In mice, efficient mitochondrial function and low reactive oxygen species (ROS) production are essential for telomere elongation during early embryogenesis. As mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes several subunits of the electron transport chain, we investigated whether mtDNA variants influence TL using a transmitochondrial cybrid model. Platelet-derived mitochondria from human donors with varying TL were introduced into mtDNA-depleted cells. Donor blood TL inversely correlated with cybrid ROS levels, suggesting that specific mtDNA variants may support telomere maintenance by enhancing mitochondrial fitness. During cybrid formation, a transient oxidative stress phase precedes cellular adaptation. At this stage, mtDNA variants associated with reduced complex I (CI) activity triggered rapid telomere shortening, which was rescued by antioxidant and NAD + precursor supplementation. Although these variants occur naturally in some individuals with long telomeres, our findings suggest that, under conditions of acute in vitro oxidative stress, CI activity is critical for preserving telomere integrity, potentially through the regulation of NAD + /NADH balance and PARP1 activity. records.title: The impact of epigenetic chemical probes: expanding targeting modalities and disease understanding
records.abstract: Small-molecule chemical modulators (chemical probes) targeting epigenetic regulators are essential tools for research by enabling precise temporal control over chromatin dynamics. Over the past two decades, large international efforts have produced hundreds of validated and openly accessible chemical probes. While the field was initially driven by occupancy-based catalytic inhibitors, there has been a recent shift toward context-dependent target engagement and induced proximity strategies. By repurposing established chemical ligands, next-generation heterobifunctional modalities (e.g., PROTACs and RIPTACs) can drive targeted protein degradation or disrupt multi-protein complexes to achieve deeper functional effects. In the present review, we discuss the evolution of epigenetic chemical probes, the emergence of induced proximity strategies, and the importance of recognizing that different targeting modalities for a given protein may yield distinct biological outcomes. Collectively, the history of epigenetic probes provides a foundation for Target 2035, an international initiative led by the Structural Genomics Consortium aimed at developing pharmacological modulators across the human proteome.

records.title: Quantitative Mass Spectrometric Analysis of 100 Plasma Proteins for the Differential Diagnosis of Multiple Myeloma and Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
affiliations: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology
Institute of Biochemical Physics NM Emanuel
records.abstract: Abstract Proteomic analysis of blood plasma is a promising tool for cancer screening. A method for screening a panel of 100 clinically significant plasma proteins using targeted mass spectrometry based on multiple reaction monitoring (MRM MS) was developed. Quantitative MRM MS analysis of plasma samples from healthy donors (N = 52) and patients with hematologic malignancies, multiple myeloma (MM; N = 35) and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DL; N = 30), was performed, and 15 proteins whose expression was significantly altered in both tumor types were identified. Using logistic regression with ElasticNet regularization, compact diagnostic panels were generated: one consisting of four proteins (BCHE, B2M, ALB, IGHM) for tumor detection (MM/DL vs. control; AUC = 0.97) and one consisting of three proteins (IGHM, VTN, IGKV4-1) for differential diagnosis of MM and DL (AUC = 0.96). The obtained results confirm the effectiveness of the multiplex MRM MS approach for the quantitative analysis of protein biomarkers. Further research and validation on larger samples are required to evaluate the clinical significance and potential for implementing the developed method in laboratory diagnostics.

records.title: KIR3DL1-based inhibitory CAR NK cell therapy alleviates on-target, off-tumor toxicity with retention of antitumor effects
records.abstract: Background Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has significantly improved outcomes in hematologic malignancies. However, its translation to solid tumors is hampered by on-target, off-tumor toxicity (OTOT) and antigen escape. These obstacles underscore the need for novel strategies that enhance antitumor efficacy while limiting OTOT. Methods We designed a NOT logic-gated CAR natural killer (NK) cell architecture that targets B7H3, a tumor-associated antigen, and endomucin (EMCN), an antigen serving as a safety marker in normal tissues. These dual CAR NK cells selectively targeted and eliminated B7H3-high tumor cells, whereas their activation was suppressed upon encountering normal cell models co-expressing B7H3 and EMCN. records.title: Glioblastoma–Neuroblastoma Cocultured Multicellular Spheroid Model for Evaluating Temozolomide Response
affiliations: Advanced Centre for Treatment, Research and Education in Cancer
records.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most lethal primary brain tumor, and its resistance to therapy is increasingly understood to arise not from tumor cells alone but also from their integration into the surrounding neural circuitry. However, no existing preclinical spheroid model isolates the direct effect of neuronal-lineage cells on glioblastoma's drug response within a rapid, scalable 3D system. We developed a heterotypic 3D coculture spheroid combining glioblastoma (U87-MG) with a neuronal-lineage surrogate population (SH-SY5Y) via the agarose liquid overlay method to directly understand this gap. Subsequently, growth, morphology, hypoxia, and temozolomide (TMZ) response over 14 days against glioblastoma only and neuroblastoma only spheroids were characterized. The coculture adopted a glioblastoma like compact, chemoresistant architecture yet, contrary to what this architecture alone would predict, it showed measurable chemosensitivity at every TMZ concentration tested, including 10 µM, a dose at which neither monoculture responded at all. This indicates that the neuronal-lineage surrogate population alters the overall TMZ response of the coculture spheroids. Drug-response data from glioblastoma only models may therefore not reflect true tumor behavior in the presence of neuronal-lineage cells, supporting the inclusion of neuronal-lineage surrogate components in preclinical glioblastoma drug screening.

records.journal: Asian Journal of Science Technology Engineering and Art
records.abstract: Green tea, derived from Camellia sinensis, is a widely consumed dietary source of bioactive polyphenols. Among its major catechins, epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) has been studied most extensively in cancer research. This review critically synthesizes phytochemical, molecular, preclinical, epidemiological, clinical, pharmacokinetic, and safety evidence to assess the potential role of green tea catechins in cancer prevention and treatment. Preclinical studies of breast, prostate, colorectal, lung, liver, oral, and hematological cancers indicate that EGCG modulates oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, proliferation, apoptosis, cell-cycle progression, angiogenesis, epithelial–mesenchymal transition, invasion, metastasis, and epigenetic regulation. Reported molecular targets include the PI3K–AKT–mTOR, MAPK, JAK–STAT, and NF-κB signaling pathways, as well as EGFR and VEGF signaling, BCL-2 family proteins, caspases, matrix metalloproteinases, and enzymes involved in DNA methylation. A systematic review and meta-analysis reported an association between green tea or EGCG exposure and lower overall cancer risk, with variation by cancer type and study design. Clinical evidence for efficacy in established malignancies remains limited, and conventional oncological treatment remains the standard of care. While mobile health (mHealth) may offer a useful approach to survivorship care, limited user involvement and scarcity of structured programs in developing countries remain barriers. METHODS: A mixed-methods study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 utilized a user-centered design framework involving 12 co-designers across nine online sessions to develop and refine the FORYOU mHealth program. records.abstract: Abstract Background We aimed to construct a curated whole-slide image (WSI)-report dataset for bladder cancer and establish a clinically grounded benchmark for evaluating vision–language models through an open community challenge. Methods We curated a dataset of 902 deidentified bladder cancer WSIs paired with corresponding pathology reports. Seven teams submitted distinct modeling frameworks. Performance was assessed using a clinically weighted composite metric integrating word-overlap scores (ROUGE-L, BLEU-4), keyword matching, and embedding-based semantic similarity. Expert mean opinion scores (MOS) were obtained, and the correlation between the weighted-sum score and expert-assigned MOS was analyzed. Results Two modeling strategies emerged: end-to-end generative architectures and multi-step classification-then-generation pipelines. Among individual submissions, the top-ranked multi-step pipeline achieved the highest main-diagnosis accuracy (48/50), whereas end-to-end models showed greater sensitivity to rare pathological features. The weighted-sum metric correlated strongly with MOS within each team (Spearman’s ρ, 0.65–0.91) and, on reports with clinically important misclassifications, agreed with MOS more closely than any single metric. Conclusions Performance variability was influenced by architectural design and the integration of pretrained foundation models. records.abstract: Background: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses. Methods: A total of 1560 patients with PTC from six hospitals were retrospectively included. The Tongji Hospital cohort was divided into training and internal validation sets, and five external cohorts were used for independent testing. Seven 2.5D tumor slices were extracted per patient, encoded with a DenseNet201 backbone, and fused by a Transformer. Model performance was compared with radiomics, ensemble learning, and multi-instance learning using AUC, calibration, decision curve, and precision-recall analyses. records.abstract: Nghiên cứu nhằm mô tả chất lượng cuộc sống của người bệnh sau phẫu thuật ung thư tuyến giáp tại Bệnh viện Nội tiết Trung ương năm 2026. Sử dụng thiết kế mô tả cắt ngang sử dụng bộ câu hỏi EORTC QLQ-C30 và THY-34 phỏng vấn 181 người bệnh ung thư tuyến giáp đã được phẫu thuật và hiện đang khám theo dõi định kỳ tại khoa Khám bệnh, Bệnh viện Nội tiết trung ương từ 01/2026-06/2026. Đối tượng nghiên cứu chủ yếu là nữ giới (86,2%), tuổi trung bình 45,1 ± 10,9; đa số mắc ung thư tuyến giáp thể nhú giai đoạn I (97,8%). Theo thang đo EORTC QLQ-C30, các lĩnh vực chức năng đạt điểm tương đối cao (75,9–85,2 điểm), điểm sức khỏe tổng quát đạt 69,1 ± 14,1; các triệu chứng nổi bật là mệt mỏi (24,3 ± 18,3), rối loạn giấc ngủ (22,7 ± 25,0) và đau (18,1 ± 16,9). Theo thang đo EORTC QLQ THY-34, các lĩnh vực có điểm cao nhất là hỗ trợ xã hội (80,9 ± 23,7), tác động xã hội (56,0 ± 29,2) và triệu chứng cảm xúc (48,5 ± 22,8); các triệu chứng đặc hiệu thường gặp nhất là triệu chứng vùng cổ (26,3 ± 17,4), vấn đề về giọng nói (21,2 ± 18,6) và khó nuốt (18,3 ± 19,0). Chất lượng cuộc sống của người bệnh sau phẫu thuật ung thư tuyến giáp nhìn chung tương đối tốt, tuy nhiên vẫn cần quan tâm cải thiện các triệu chứng thể chất, tâm lý và xã hội.

Owing to the lack of free 5′ and 3′ ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotemporal expression specificity. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. records.title: Cognitive biases and their associations with psychopathology among children with cancer
records.abstract: Childhood cancers are life-threatening diseases and are a major cause of death in children worldwide. Research shows that children with cancer are at risk for psychopathology, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety and depression. Major theories of psychopathology assign a significant role to the way people attend to and remember negative content as predictors and maintenance factors in emotional disorders. Thus, the aim of the proposed research is to delineate factors that may predict psychopathology among children with cancer. In line with central theories of emotional disorders (Mathews & MacLeod, 2005), we focus on cognitive biases involving processing threat-related information, and their relation to psychopathology. The children in the active phase of the treatment and those in remission will perform several cognitive tasks, assessing attention bias, working memory bias, and memory bias. Biases will involve stimuli related with cancer, non-cancer negative and neutral. These types of stimuli were chosen to explore whether the biases are specific to stimuli that are related to the acquired illness. Subsequently, they will be interviewed using semi-structured clinical interviews to assess the presence of emotional disorders. Finally, they will complete a set of questionnaires assessing symptom severity of depression, anxiety, and PTSD. For a control group we will have a healthy children group. records.abstract: Long-term psoriasis management remains a major challenge worldwide. Although repeated imiquimod (IMQ) application has been used to mimic psoriatic inflammatory reactivation, it remains unclear whether this approach reflects amplified acute inflammation or the emergence of tissue-resident, memory-associated features. Here, we established a repeated IMQ-challenge model (IMQ-R) and compared it with a single-course IMQ model (IMQ-S) and human psoriatic lesions using bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (single-cell RNA-seq). During the final induction phase, IMQ-R showed a more rapid re-emergence of skin inflammation than IMQ-S and displayed features of inflammatory reactivation in previously challenged skin, including IL-17-related pathways, TRM-related T-cell features, and predicted multicellular communication patterns. Single-cell analysis showed that IMQ-R exhibited a cellular composition more similar to active human psoriatic skin than IMQ-S, with keratinocyte (KC) expansion, endothelial cell (EC) enrichment, and relative preservation of T-cell populations. T-cell subsets with memory-associated annotations, including central memory T cells (TCM) and tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM), were increased in IMQ-R.
